title: Tenant-aware slab reclaimer with paging hysteresis and spillback failsafe
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation: In multi-tenant production workloads we observed sustained KV cache fragmentation and oscillating spill events during load spikes. This behavior amplifies tail-latency for inference requests because active prefixes get evicted during aggressive global reclamation and continuous batching bursts interfere with reclamation quiesce points. The goal of this PR is to reduce fragmentation-driven spillovers and eviction-induced latency spikes by introducing a tenant-aware slab reclamation policy and a paging hysteresis guard that prevents thrash.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a tenant-prioritized slab reclaimer that prefers cold-tenant segments, integrates a hysteresis window around page reclamation (avoid immediate reclaim after short-lived spikes), introduces a spillback failsafe to gracefully throttle new allocations when spill rates exceed a threshold, and wires these behaviors into the runtime scheduler and continuous-batching quiesce points. Also adds metrics and dashboards for visibility and synthetic benchmarks used for validation.

Design highlights: - Tenant scoring: each tenant is scored based on recent access heat (EWMA of lookups and prefix hits), write pressure, and resident fraction. The reclaimer targets slabs with the lowest tenant-weighted residency score. - Hysteresis window: reclamation of newly-created pages is deferred for a configurable hysteresis period (default 10s) to prevent reclaiming pages that were created during a short burst. - Spillback failsafe: if spill events/sec > 5 for > 30s, the allocator enters a soft-fallback that reduces per-tenant allocation pace and routes new requests to a higher-latency but lower-memory model variant (configurable policy). This avoids hard OOM and maintains availability. - Continuous batching interaction: introduced a batching quiesce hook so reclamation only runs between batch drain points; this prevents mid-batch eviction of KV entries needed by the same request. - Kernel hinting: added lightweight metadata to mark compacted slabs so the runtime kernel selector favors fast-path lookup kernels when accessing compacted regions.

Implementation notes: - New package: internal/kv/reclaimer containing TenantReclaimer, HysteresisTracker, and SpillbackController (core algorithms implemented in ~280 lines). - Integrations: runtime/scheduler to register quiesce hooks; serving/runtime allocator to consult SpillbackController before admitting large allocations; observability to emit kv.reclaimer.* metrics and tenant.breakdown.*. - Tests: unit tests for hysteresis logic, tenant scoring, and spillback transitions; integration test with 5-tenent load generator simulating bursty writes.

Benchmark results (staging cluster, G4dn-like hardware): - Baseline (main, before change): median L40 token latency 36ms, p95 210ms, spill events/day: 1,280. - After PR (default config): median 34ms, p95 120ms (43% reduction), spill events/day: 410 (68% reduction), steady-state throughput within 3% of baseline. - Cost: memory headroom increased by ~12% after compaction cycles, reducing emergency spill frequency.

Checklist: - [x] Algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Integration tests and perf harness updated - [x] CI green after flaky test rerun - [x] Metrics & dashboards added - [x] Docs (internal ops runbook) updated

Safety and rollout: default configuration is conservative (hysteresis=10s, spillback threshold conservative) and feature is behind a runtime config flag (kv.tenant_reclaimer.enabled=false by default). Rollout plan: enable on one region with canary capacity, monitor kv.reclaimer.spill_rate and tenant.p95_latency for 48 hours before wide rollout.

Files changed (high-level): internal/kv/reclaimer/reclaimer.go (new), internal/kv/reclaimer/hysteresis.go (new), internal/kv/reclaimer/spillback.go (new), runtime/scheduler/quiesce_hooks.go (mod), serving/allocator/tenant_allocator.go (mod), serving/allocator/allocator_metrics_test.go (new tests), integration/perf/kv_multi_tenant_loadtest.go (new), docs/ops/kv-reclaimer.md (new), dashboards/kv-reclaimer.json (new), go.mod (tweak). Small illustrative change: in quiesce_hooks.go we add: 

  // before: no-op 
  func RunQuiesceHooks() { /* drain batches */ } 
  // after: register tenant reclaimer to run between batch drains 
  func RunQuiesceHooks() { /* drain batches */ tenantReclaimer.RunCycle() }

Review thread summary (single-string conversational transcript): 
Reviewer: Asha Patel - "This looks promising. Can we make the hysteresis tunable per-tenant? Some tenants have short-lived bursts that we shouldn't penalize long-term." 
Author: Jordan Lee - "Agree; made hysteresis per-tenant with a global ceiling in the latest commit (hysteresis is min(global, tenant_bias*10s))." 
Reviewer: Diego Rivera - "Can we ensure the spillback policy doesn't route sensitive tenants to lower-quality models automatically? We need an allowlist." 
Author: Jordan Lee - "Added allowlist support and a second-tier policy flag kv.spillback.allowlist. Default behavior is opt-in; sensitive tenants must be explicitly configured." 
Reviewer: Marta Kline - "Found a flaky test in allocator_metrics_test on macOS runners, it's timing-sensitive." 
Author: Jordan Lee - "Adjusted test timing and added deterministic clock in tests; reran CI." 
Reviewer: Samir Gupta - "Approach LGTM, but please add a note in release notes about possible transient increase in eviction count during the first compaction cycle." 
Author: Jordan Lee - "Added release note and ops runbook guidance." 

CI: initial pipeline had a transient failure in allocator_metrics_test (timing), which was fixed in commit 3; final CI run passed (linux/amd64, linux/arm, integration perf harness).

Merge: squash-merged to main after approvals and perf sign-off.

Related work and follow-ups: - Follow-up: expose per-tenant hysteresis tuning in Console + UI (ENG-2145) - Follow-up: move spillback policy into routing layer for more granular fallbacks (ENG-2201)

Note: description is intentionally detailed to aid reviewers and on-call engineers during rollout.
